cards.answer: A Miden account is a small program that holds assets and has rules, such as who must approve a payment. An account ID is the unique code that identifies your account. A Miden address points to your account, so people can send to you. A Mainnet address starts with mm1 and a Testnet address starts with mtst1. An address has a built-in check that helps catch typing mistakes, but it cannot show that it belongs to the right person. Your account ID, a note's sender and the fact that a transaction happened are public. Check that an address is for the network you are using before you send.

cards.pick: public vs private account type
cards.answer: A Miden account is public or private, fixed when it is created. A public account's data is openly visible on the network. With a private account, your balance and holdings are not published on the public chain. A Bread Guardian account is private; some imported accounts can be public. To use a private account, you need your keys and a current copy of its data. Private does not hide your account ID. Assume your Guardian company can see your account and payments. Today all three validators, computers that check transactions, receive each transaction's private details.

cards.pick: undo a payment? can I be blocked?
cards.answer: Bread cannot reverse a transaction you approved. If a payment has a take-back date and is not accepted, you may be able to take it back after that date. If your Guardian, a service that must approve payments, is down or refuses, your payments stop, and you may not be able to switch right away. Bread blocks all wallet access, even withdrawals, from some places. During partner mainnet, the network operator can halt the network and rewind it, which may undo payments you sent or received. The operator can also block addresses. USDCx can be blocked for an address, and it can be paused.

cards.pick: Mainnet vs Testnet; test tokens
cards.answer: Mainnet is the live network, where assets are real. Testnet is for practice with test tokens that have no money value. A test network can be reset, which clears balances and history. Test balances never carry over to Mainnet. Bread may ask for a Mainnet access code for a new wallet, so follow what the app shows. Mainnet is currently an early, closed partner network run by a single network operator. Anything sent from a real network to a test address is lost. Switching a test wallet to Mainnet clears this wallet, its balances and history from the device, so save your recovery details first.

cards.pick: what is Bread; what can I do; custody
cards.answer: Bread is a wallet app for Miden, a network for digital money and assets. Self-custody means the company behind Bread cannot move your assets. You can send and receive money; swaps, bridges and Earn depend on region and version. In Bread, a Guardian is an online service, usually run by a company. A standard new account uses a Guardian, which keeps a copy of your account data. Assume the company running your Guardian can see your account and payments. Keep your 12-word recovery phrase safe: Bread cannot recover it. Bread and Miden are early-stage, so do not use money you cannot afford to lose.

cards.pick: what the assistant receives and can do
cards.answer: The Bread assistant answers questions and prepares actions, like a send, for you to review. In help answers, the assistant cannot see your account or check a payment. Balance and history answers are worked out on your device. Your messages go to Bread's AI service and the AI provider behind it. Some context can go too, like the last help topic or an unfinished action. Bread first tries to hide addresses, contact names, amounts and some token names. This can miss details, so leave out anything private. Never type your recovery phrase, private keys, password or passcode into this chat.

cards.pick: connect sites or apps; safe; disconnect
cards.answer: A connected site gets your account ID. It can ask for private data and ask you to approve actions. Some permissions let it read private data without asking again, so read the connect screen. To disconnect a site, find it under "Authorized DApps", "See connected", and choose "Disconnect". If a site will not connect, check your internet and that it uses your wallet's network. Never type your recovery phrase, private keys or password into a site. Only connect sites you trust. A bad request that you approve can lose money. Disconnecting cannot take back data a site got or undo what you approved.

cards.pick: which phones, browsers or computers work
cards.answer: Bread is offered as a Chrome browser extension, an iPhone app and an Android app. The help center says other browsers and platforms are not supported right now. Features can differ between platforms and app versions. Get Bread only from official sources, such as the store links at support.miden.xyz.

cards.pick: invite or access code; code not working
cards.answer: If Bread asks for an access code for a new wallet, use the code from your invite email. Choose "I have a code" and enter it exactly, including capital and small letters. A Mainnet account you already registered needs no new code: use "Recover your account". For a standard account, this needs your 12-word recovery phrase and your Guardian's copy of your account data. If you have no invite or the code does not work, contact support at support.miden.xyz. Do not reset or delete a working wallet just to enter a code. Keep your code private: leave it out of posts, screenshots and support reports.

cards.pick: reach a person; what can support do
cards.answer: For help, contact Bread support at support.miden.xyz. Support can help you look into a problem, such as tracing a swap or bridge transfer, but cannot promise a fix. When you contact support, include your device model, system version, app version and what happened, with no secrets. This chat cannot contact support for you or open a ticket. Never share your recovery phrase, private keys, password, passcode or wallet file with anyone, including support. Bread support cannot reset your password, recover your recovery phrase, recover funds on your behalf or reverse a transaction you approved.

cards.pick: no card answers the question
cards.answer: I don't know the answer to that. For help with your wallet, go to support.miden.xyz. Never share your recovery phrase.

cards.pick: unmatched error or money problem
cards.answer: I can't tell what went wrong from here. Don't reset or delete Bread. If it was a payment, don't send it again while you are unsure what happened to it. Open it in Activity and read its message. For help, go to support.miden.xyz. Never share your recovery phrase.
